name: binharness
description: Reverse engineer stripped Nintendo Switch modules (NSO/NRO/NSP) and any binary: hex viewer, AArch64 disassembly, function/RTTI/syscall/service recovery, NPDM parsing, and Ghidra/IDA export.
author: dougchansan
systemPrompt: You have the binharness tools (mcp__binharness__*) for reverse engineering Nintendo Switch modules (NSO/NRO; AArch64, base 0x7100000000) and any binary. These sysmodules are stripped and statically linked, so recover names first. On a fresh module run, in order: file_info, parse_npdm (identity + which services it hosts/uses + syscall allowlist), label_rtti (names C++ classes, vtables and virtual methods), then label_syscalls, label_services and label_from_strings. After that list_functions/find_rtti/scan_syscalls/find_services come back named; use find_string_refs to reach specific logic, disassemble (by address or symbol) plus call_graph and find_xrefs to follow it. view_binary opens the hex viewer. extract_image + export_symbols hand off to Ghidra/IDA. Prefer small targeted calls; cite virtual addresses as hex strings. NCA files are encrypted and cannot be decrypted — ask for extracted NSO/NRO.
skillInstructions: When the user wants to inspect, disassemble or reverse engineer a binary (especially a Switch NSO/NRO), load the binharness skill and follow its recon-first workflow.

interface.shortDescription: Reverse engineer Switch modules and binaries
interface.longDescription: A reverse-engineering toolkit for stripped Nintendo Switch modules (NSO/NRO/NSP/XCI) and any binary. Opens an interactive hex viewer, disassembles AArch64, recovers function boundaries, C++ class names (RTTI), syscall wrappers and IPC services, parses NPDM metadata, and exports every recovered name as Ghidra and IDA import scripts.
tryPrompts: Open this .bin in the hex viewer
What does this Switch NSO module do? Recover its functions and services.
Disassemble the entry point and reconstruct it in C

binharness.description: Hex viewer, NSO/NRO/NSP parsing, AArch64 disassembly, function/RTTI/syscall/service recovery, and Ghidra/IDA export. Runs locally via Node; reads files only.
